thm-local-finite-element-interpolation-estimates, theorem: “Assume Countable Choice. Let $k\ge0$, $1\le p<\infty$, and let
$(\widehat S_d,\widehat P,\widehat\Sigma)$ be a reference finite element
whose polynomial space contains $\mathbb P_k$. Assume its degrees of
freedom are bounded on $W^{\ell,p}(\widehat S_d)$ for an integer
$\ell\ge1$, let $r,m\in\mathbb N_0$, and let $\widehat I$ be its
interpolant. Thus
$\widehat Iq=q$ for $q\in\mathbb P_k$. On a shape-regular affine mesh
as in [[def-matching-affine-simplicial-meshes]], for each cell $K$ with its
orientation-preserving reference map $F_K$ define
$$I_Kv=(\widehat I(v\circ F_K))\circ F_K^{-1}.$$
For every such cell, if $\ell\le r\le k+1$ and $0\le m\le r$, then for
$v\in W^{r,p}(K)$,
$$|v-I_Kv|_{W^{m,p}(K)}\le C h_K^{r-m}|v|_{W^{r,p}(K)}.$$
If $\ell>k+1$ and $0\le m\le k+1$, then for $v\in W^{\ell,p}(K)$,
$$|v-I_Kv|_{W^{m,p}(K)} \le C\sum_{n=k+1}^{\ell}h_K^{n-m}|v|_{W^{n,p}(K)}.$$
The constants are uniform over the mesh family and depend on the stated
reference element, exponents and shape-regularity bound. For Lagrange
elements, the boundedness hypothesis on the nodal functionals is supplied
by [[thm-lagrange-point-evaluation-threshold-on-reference-simplex]] when
$\ell>d/p$; unisolvence of a particular node set is a separate hypothesis.”

thm-cea-quasi-optimality-for-conforming-galerkin-approximations, theorem: “Assume Countable Choice. Let $V$ be a real or complex Hilbert space and let
$a:V\times V\to\mathbb K$ be linear in its first argument, conjugate-linear
in its second, bounded by $M$, and coercive with constant $\alpha>0$:
$$|a(v,w)|\le M\|v\|_V\|w\|_V,\qquad \operatorname{Re}a(v,v)\ge\alpha\|v\|_V^2.$$
Let $F:V\to\mathbb K$ be bounded and conjugate-linear, and let $V_h\subseteq V$
be finite-dimensional. Then there are unique $u\in V$ and $u_h\in V_h$ with
$$a(u,v)=F(v)\quad(v\in V).$$
$$a(u_h,v_h)=F(v_h)\quad(v_h\in V_h).$$
The solutions satisfy
$$\|u-u_h\|_V\le\frac M\alpha\inf_{v_h\in V_h}\|u-v_h\|_V.$$
The real bilinear case uses linear functionals and reads $\operatorname{Re}$ as
the identity.”

original.source_excerpt:
def-coordinatewise-product-moment-functional, definition: “For $d\ge1$, let $(a_j,b_j,m_j,2m_j-1,\mu_j)$ be Gaussian moment data for
each coordinate $j=1,\ldots,d$, and write
$M^{(j)}_k:=\int x^k\,d\mu_j(x)$. A **coordinatewise tensor polynomial** is a
finite coefficient family $(c_\alpha)$ indexed by multi-indices
$\alpha=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_d)$ with
$0\le\alpha_j\le2m_j-1$, evaluated by
$$ P(x_1,\ldots,x_d)=\sum_{\alpha}c_\alpha\prod_{j=1}^{d}x_j^{\alpha_j}. $$
Define its **coordinatewise product-moment value** by
$$ I_\otimes(P):=\sum_{\alpha}c_\alpha\prod_{j=1}^{d}M^{(j)}_{\alpha_j}. $$
The coefficient family is part of the formal polynomial data, so this finite
sum is unambiguous. This definition specifies the product-moment functional
used for coordinatewise exactness without requiring a measure-product
construction.”

def-tensor-product-gauss-rule, definition: “Let $d\ge1$ and, for each coordinate $j=1,\ldots,d$, let
$Q_j(f)=\sum_{i=1}^{m_j}w_i^{(j)}f(x_i^{(j)})$ be a well-defined Gaussian rule
as in [[def-gauss-quadrature-rule]] and
[[lem-gauss-quadrature-rule-data-well-defined]]. Its **tensor-product
quadrature rule** is
$$ Q_{\otimes}(f):= \sum_{i_1=1}^{m_1}\cdots\sum_{i_d=1}^{m_d} \left(\prod_{j=1}^{d}w_{i_j}^{(j)}\right) f\left(x_{i_1}^{(1)},\ldots,x_{i_d}^{(d)}\right). $$
Its node set is the Cartesian product of the one-dimensional node sets; the
displayed finite sum is its value on any function defined on that node set.”

thm-gauss-rule-exact-through-degree-2m-minus-1-and-positive-weights, theorem: “Let $(a,b,m,2m-1,\mu)$ be moment data as in
[[def-gauss-moment-data]], and let $Q_m$ and $w_i$ be the rule and weights of
[[def-gauss-quadrature-rule]]. For every real polynomial $f$ of degree at most
$2m-1$,
$$ \int_{[a,b]} f(x)\,d\mu(x)=Q_m(f)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_if(x_i). $$
Moreover, $w_i>0$ for every $i$ and $\sum_iw_i=\mu([a,b])$.”

thm-tensor-product-gauss-exactness-and-exponential-node-count, theorem: “For $d\ge1$, take one-dimensional Gaussian rules $Q_j$ with orders $m_j$ and
moment data $(a_j,b_j,m_j,2m_j-1,\mu_j)$, and form their tensor rule
$Q_\otimes$ as in [[def-tensor-product-gauss-rule]]. For every coordinatewise
tensor polynomial $P$ of [[def-coordinatewise-product-moment-functional]],
$$ Q_\otimes(P)=I_\otimes(P). $$
The tensor rule has exactly $\prod_{j=1}^{d}m_j$ distinct nodes. In particular,
using the same $m\ge2$ nodes in each coordinate requires $m^d$ node
evaluations, exponential growth in $d$.”

original.source_excerpt:
def-smolyak-cubature, definition: “Fix a dimension $d\ge1$. A finite set $\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb N_0^d$ is
**downward closed** if, whenever $\ell\in\Lambda$ and $\ell_j>0$, the index
$\ell-e_j$ also belongs to $\Lambda$; here $e_j$ is the $j$th coordinate unit
vector. In this pair an admissible Smolyak set is a nonempty finite downward-
closed $\Lambda$ that contains $0$.

For a level hierarchy from [[def-smolyak-univariate-level-hierarchy]], define
the **Smolyak cubature functional**
$$Q_\Lambda(f):=\sum_{\ell\in\Lambda}(\Delta_{\ell_1}^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes\Delta_{\ell_d}^{(d)})(f).$$
Each summand is a finite signed weighted sum. Expanding all differences and
adding coefficients at equal points gives one finite signed weight for each
distinct node in
$$\mathcal N_\Lambda:=\bigcup_{\ell\in\Lambda}X_{\ell_1}\times\cdots\times X_{\ell_d}.$$
The **node-union work count** for this direct evaluation convention is
$W(\Lambda):=|\mathcal N_\Lambda|$, so shared nodes are counted once. A
combined weight may be negative or zero; no positivity claim follows from the
definition.”

lem-smolyak-mixed-simpson-detail-decay, lemma: “Let $d\ge1$. For $S=\{j_1<\cdots<j_k\}\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}$, define
$$D_Sf:=\partial_{x_{j_k}}^4\cdots\partial_{x_{j_1}}^4f,$$
so these derivatives are applied in increasing coordinate order; set
$D_\varnothing f=f$. Assume every $D_Sf$ is continuous on the closed cube,
with the one-sided endpoint convention of
[[def-higher-derivatives-and-smoothness]], and choose finite bounds $M_S\ge0$
such that $|D_Sf(x)|\le M_S$ on $[0,1]^d$. For
$\ell\in\mathbb N_0^d$, put $S(\ell):=\{j:\ell_j\ge1\}$ and
$$\delta_\ell(f):=(\Delta_{\ell_1}^{(1)}\otimes\cdots\otimes\Delta_{\ell_d}^{(d)})(f).$$
Then
$$|\delta_\ell(f)|\le M_{S(\ell)}\left(\frac{17}{2880}\right)^{|S(\ell)|}16^{-\sum_{j\in S(\ell)}\ell_j}.$$
Moreover, for every finite $F\subseteq\mathbb N_0^d$,
$$\sum_{\ell\in F}|\delta_\ell(f)|\le\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}}M_S\left(\frac{17}{43200}\right)^{|S|}<\infty.$$”

thm-smolyak-isotropic-mixed-smoothness-work-error-rate, theorem: “Let $d\ge1$, $n\ge2d$, and let $f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R$ satisfy the
continuous mixed fourth-derivative hypotheses and bounds $M_S$ of
[[lem-smolyak-mixed-simpson-detail-decay]]. Define the isotropic index set
$$\Lambda_n:=\{\ell\in\mathbb N_0^d:|\ell|_1\le n\},$$
and let $W_{n,d}:=|\mathcal N_{\Lambda_n}|$ be the distinct-node work count
of [[def-smolyak-cubature]] and [[alg-smolyak-node-deduplication]]. For a
dyadic node $x$, let $t(x)=0$ for $x=0,1,1/2$; if $x=p/2^{r+1}$ is interior
and reduced with odd numerator $p$, let $t(x)=r\ge1$. Put
$$a_0:=3,\qquad a_r:=2^r\ (r\ge1),$$
$$\|f\|_{\mathrm{mix},d}:=\sum_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}}\left(\frac{17}{2880}\right)^{|S|}M_S,\quad T_d:=\sup_{N\ge1}\sum_{r=1}^{N}r^{d-1}16^{-r},$$
$$D_d:=2\cdot3^d d^{d-1},\qquad C_d:=D_d^4T_d\left(\frac3{\log 2}\right)^{5(d-1)},$$

def-chebyshev-gauss-lobatto-collocation-grid: “Let $N\ge1$ be an integer and put $x_j=\cos(j\pi/N)$ for $j=0,\ldots,N$. The ordering is decreasing: $x_0=1$ and $x_N=-1$. These are the Chebyshev–Gauss–Lobatto nodes; [[thm-chebyshev-multiple-angle-identities]] gives $T_N(x_j)=(-1)^j$. They are distinct because cosine is strictly decreasing on $[0,\pi]$ by [[thm-sine-cosine-signs-monotonicity-and-ranges]].

For interpolation using [[def-cardinal-polynomial-interpolation]], use the increasing reindexing $z_k=x_{N-k}$, $k=0,\ldots,N$. For descending-grid data $U_j$, the corresponding increasing data are $Y_k=U_{N-k}$.

For nodal data $U_0,\ldots,U_N$, define $I_N^LU$ to be the cardinal interpolant of $(Y_k)_{k=0}^N$ at $(z_k)_{k=0}^N$. For a function $f$ defined on the interval, write $I_N^Lf$ for the interpolant of its nodal values. The increasing-node interpolation theorem [[thm-cardinal-polynomial-interpolant-exists-uniquely]] makes this polynomial unique.”

lem-chebyshev-lobatto-mode-aliasing: “Let $N\ge1$, let $x_j=\cos(j\pi/N)$, and let $I_N^L$ denote degree-at-most-$N$ interpolation on these nodes. For every integer $n\ge0$, let $\rho_N(n)$ be the unique integer $r\in\{0,\ldots,N\}$ congruent to either $n$ or $-n$ modulo $2N$. Then
$$
I_N^L T_n=T_{\rho_N(n)}.
$$
In particular, sampling a Chebyshev series on the Lobatto grid can fold every degree $n>N$ to a degree at most $N$.”

thm-chebyshev-lobatto-interpolation-rate-under-spectral-sobolev-regularity: “Let $s>1/2$, $N\ge1$, and $u=\sum_{n\ge0}c_nT_n\in H_C^s$. Then the series converges uniformly, its nodal interpolant $I_N^Lu$ is defined, and
$$
\|u-I_N^Lu\|_C\le C_sN^{-s}\|u\|_{H_C^s},\qquad
C_s=1+2\sqrt{1+\frac1{2s-1}}.
$$”

def-weighted-orthogonal-polynomial-galerkin-space: “Let $\mu$ be a finite positive Borel measure on a compact interval $[a,b]$ with infinite relative support. For each integer $N\ge0$, the moment data $(a,b,m=N+1,r=2N+1,\mu)$ satisfy the hypotheses of [[def-gauss-moment-data]]. Let $p_0,\ldots,p_N$ be the monic orthogonal polynomials supplied by [[thm-monic-gauss-orthogonal-polynomials-exist-uniquely]], and write
$$
h_n=\int_{[a,b]}p_n(x)^2\,d\mu(x)>0.
$$
The finite-dimensional weighted Galerkin space is
$$
V_N(\mu)=\operatorname{span}\{p_0,\ldots,p_N\}\subset L^2(\mu).
$$
Here $L^2(\mu)$ means measurable functions with finite integral of the squared absolute value, modulo equality $\mu$-almost everywhere.

For a coefficient sequence $(c_n)_{n\ge0}$ with $\sum_{n\ge0}(1+n^2)^s|c_n|^2h_n<\infty$, define its weighted spectral Sobolev norm by
$$
\left\|\sum_{n\ge0}c_np_n\right\|_{H^s_\mu}^2
=\sum_{n\ge0}(1+n^2)^s|c_n|^2h_n,\qquad s\ge0.
$$
The associated orthogonal Galerkin projection is $\Pi_N(\sum_{n\ge0}c_np_n)=\sum_{n=0}^Nc_np_n$. This coefficient-defined scale is specific to the weight $\mu$ and the selected orthogonal-polynomial family; no equivalence with a derivative-based Sobolev norm is asserted here.”

thm-weighted-orthogonal-polynomial-galerkin-projection-is-well-defined: “Under the hypotheses of [[def-weighted-orthogonal-polynomial-galerkin-space]], for every real measurable $u$ such that $\int|u p_j|\,d\mu<\infty$ for $0\le j\le N$, the formula
$$
\Pi_Nu=\sum_{j=0}^{N}\frac{\int u(x)p_j(x)\,d\mu(x)}{h_j}\,p_j
$$
is finite and defines the unique element of $V_N(\mu)$ whose residual is orthogonal to every $p_i$, $0\le i\le N$.”
